units: metres, +Z up, Blender = Unreal x 100 (cm); Unreal Y = -Blender Y (FBX axis conversion by Scripts/pipeline)

stairs.reference: References/Dojo/dojo_landscape_ref.png (the stone stair path, lower left)

rail_line.post_base_line: z = R (y_flight / T + 1/2): the tread midpoints; posts stand mid-tread

grid.rotation: any multiple of 90 deg about Z; all pieces are built on +Y (walking up / along +Y)

how_to_chain: flight -> flight: next.loc = this.loc + R(rot) (0, run, rise), same rot (a longer straight flight)
flight -> landing (W x W): landing.loc = flight.out + R(rot) (0, W/2, 0)
landing -> flight straight on: flight.loc = landing.loc + R(rot) (0, W/2, 0); right turn: + R(rot) (W/2, 0, 0) with flight rot = rot - 90; left turn: - R(rot) (W/2, 0, 0) with rot + 90

turn landing (LandingL): at the landing's rot it takes a RIGHT turn (arrive over S, leave over E); for a LEFT turn give it rot - 90 (arrive S, leave W). f1: every landing is flush paving to its edges (no curbs), so Landing and LandingL differ only in their flag layout and snaps
switchback (LandingSB): loc = arriving flight.out + R(rot) ((W + 0.4)/2, W/2, 0); the departing flight pivot = landing.loc + R(rot) ((W + 0.4)/2, -W/2, 0), rot + 180; a Cheek between them at x = 0

rails (the rail line is inset T/2 = 1/6 m from every edge, so corners land exactly on the grid). f1: Rail_Slope_Rxxx carries the posts at BOTH its ends (a run never cantilevers): place it at flight.loc + R(rot) (+-(W/2 - 1/6), -1/6, 0). f2: round posts with rounded tops, SQUARED rails housed into them. Rail_Flat_L{W} / Rail_Flat_T{W} are the two squared rails alone, hung between posts that other pieces supply: on a landing between two flights the slope below's end post and the slope above's start post (span W exactly); round an OUTSIDE turn: Rail_Flat_L{W} to a Rail_CornerPost, then Rail_Flat_T{W} (W - 1/3) turned 90 deg to the next slope's start post; a flat run that starts or ends the rail (or joins two flat spans) takes a Rail_EndPost. Two slopes chained with no landing between share one post position: prefer the longer slope piece (R100 + R100 = R200); if both are used the coincident posts are identical geometry

cheeks: Cheek_Rxxx at flight.loc + R(rot) (+-(W/2 + 0.2), 0, 0): one dressed stone per tread standing +0.15 over it on a base of rounded wall stones; Cheek_L{W} along landing sides (+0.15 over the paving); f2: Cheek_Low_Rxxx / Cheek_Low_L{W} = the SINGLE-COURSE low variant (+0.12, 0.22 m in the soil, no base), same placement; CheekCorner where two meet at 90 deg. Moss sits where the cheek meets the soil. Reference-matching paths use the cheek on the cliff side only (or none) and natural rock

kerbs (f2): Stair_Kerb_L{060,120,180} = low edging of squared blocks (+0.07 over the path), pivot on its centre line at path level, running +Y, outer (soil) side +X: along a landing / path edge at x = +-(W/2 + 0.115) (rot 0 on the +X edge, rot 180 from the far end on the -X edge); Stair_Kerb_Corner closes two kerbs at 90 deg. The reference edges its paths and landings with them on the open side

lanterns: Lantern_Timber is the reference's path lantern: ONE per landing (never two side by side), on the cliff side, >= 0.5 m clear of any rail line and of any rail's plan (its eave is 0.44 m wide, top 1.31 m: a rail must never run into its roof); Lantern_Stone is a kit extra, not in the reference path

grid.datum: Z 0 = terrace grade (the dojo ground plane, the coping top); walls hang down
grid.pivot: face line at grade at the module start; face -> local -Y; fill -> +Y
grid.tooth_rule: course k (COURSE_S) runs +TOOTH (even k) / -TOOTH (odd k) past the grid line at both ends of every piece: neighbours interlock

straight.corner_flare: none (the sangi-zumi follow the straight batter)

sweep.pieces: *_Sweep (Wall_{2m,4m}_H{3,4,6}, CornerOut, CornerIn, EndL, EndR, WallFoot_CornerOut / _CornerIn at H 3 / 4 / 6)
sweep.corner_flare: outside corners: +0.005 s^2 outward at the arris, fading over 1.4 m

batter.mixing: never butt a straight piece against a Sweep piece of the same height: their faces part by 0.035 s^2 below grade; switch profiles only at a corner or an end

assembly.straight: place at the previous piece's 'end' snap, same yaw; walls of different H may sit side by side (same face profile; the taller one's end below the shorter's foot is closed by core + stones, cover it with terrain or a foot skirt)
assembly.corner: CornerOut: next pivot (1, 1, 0) yaw +90; CornerIn (every straight-profile height and CornerIn_H3/H4_Sweep): next pivot (2, -2, 0) yaw -90; CornerIn_H6_Sweep: next pivot (3, -3, 0) yaw -90 (a 3 m arm: the sweep pulls the corner line in 1.86 m at the 6 m foot); WallCoping_CornerIn: (2, -2, 0)
assembly.ends: EndL starts a run (its 'end' snap feeds the first module), EndR closes one (placed at the last module's 'end'); both return 1.2 m into the slope
assembly.foot: WallFoot_* at each wall piece's 'foot' snap (same yaw): ONE continuous level footing course, tops +0.06 over the nominal foot, 0.10 proud of the face, buried to -0.45 (f2: no skirt, no loose rubble); a Sweep wall takes the *_Sweep corner feet
assembly.coping_alone: WallCoping_* has the walls' top course alone (pivot at grade, same face line)
assembly.dojo_wall_on_top: kit 1's perimeter wall stands on the coping: its outer footing face 0.10 m behind the coping arris (local y = +0.10 .. +1.10 for the 1.0 m kit-1 wall); its footing sits at grade (kit 1 Z 0 = terrace Z 0); the dojo apron / paving meets the coping top flush at Z 0 behind y = 0.55
assembly.stair_opening: Wall_StairOpening_H{2,3,4}: a 4 m module; the stair path (track 9) continues from 'stair_foot' on the ground and 'stair_top' on the terrace; taller walls: split the climb (a 4 m opening on a lower terrace, or track 9's flights on the slope)
assembly.gasp: walls are not walkable (straight batter 84.3 deg; Sweep 84-62 deg): only coping tops, landings, steps and curbs are; H2 (2.0 m) is inside GASP's 2.75 m mantle ceiling, H3+ are not; traversal needs LevelBlock_Traversable markers placed in the level (GASP_TRAVERSAL.md)
